fichas.title: Rainwater drainage and unpressurised drainage
fichas.summary: Roof rainwater is conveyed by a pipe system, preferably to on-plot percolation. Each roof requires at least one downpipe and one emergency overflow with free discharge; rainwater must not enter soil stacks. Pipes are designed for local rainfall, with emergency overflow and pressure-relief measures to limit damage from overloading. The page gives discharge factors for surface types and guidance for unpressurised pipe sizing, filling and falls.
uses: Limit damage from heavy rainfall and pipe overloading
Determine rainwater run-off using surface discharge factors
